name: Comic book halftone
means: Four-colour newsprint comic art: heavy black ink outline and solid spot blacks carrying the drawing, colour laid in as visible Ben-Day dot screens rather than solid fills, and the plates slightly out of register so a thin cyan or magenta fringe shows along the black line.
prose: a 1970s four-colour comic book page printed on newsprint, heavy black ink outlines and solid spot blacks, colour applied as coarse visible Ben-Day halftone dots rather than flat fills, the colour plates slightly misregistered so thin cyan and magenta fringes show against the black line, limited flat primary palette, absorbent paper stock
negative_add: photorealistic, smooth gradient, airbrush, anime, cel shading, 3d
works_for: Stills yes, video poorly. INFERRED from the flat-survives/texture-boils rule, not measured here: the dot screen is pixel-scale texture, which is the class LTX-2.3 boils, so a halftone keyframe tends to animate into a crawling moire. If you need it moving, hold the still and move the frame in post rather than letting i2v interpolate the dots.
note: Dot SCALE is the whole failure mode. Ask for coarse visible Ben-Day dots by name or the model renders a fine grey screen that disappears entirely at 1344x768, leaving a flat comic with no print idiom at all. NOT AVAILABLE on animagine: 'western comic' sits in this project's standing negative precisely because it returns anime eyes on comic anatomy (studio/tags/western_comic.json), so the tags field is deliberately empty rather than tempting. The anime checkpoint does have a native halftone idiom, but it is the Japanese one - 'manga, screentone, halftone, monochrome' gives screentone, a different style, and studio/tags/monochrome.json measured that monochrome greyscales the entire frame, so that route is black and white only. Do not mistake this for a look: the misregistration fringe has to be DRAWN, and no ffmpeg grade in studio/looks/ can add ink that was never printed. | ENGINE CORRECTED anime -> qwen: Only partly rescued, and the LoRA that does it is qwen-based, so the engine follows it. Left status=weak: manga_screentone produces a real dot screen unaided and remains the better card.
verdict: THE COMIC ARRIVES; THE HALFTONE DOES NOT. Without a LoRA this is still a photograph sitting inside a newsprint-paper frame with a cyan and magenta fringe on the frame edge, and no dot screen anywhere in the image. With illustration-1.0-qwen-image at 1.0 the photograph becomes a real inked drawing - heavy black outline, spot blacks, drawn hair, paper-toned ground, and a thin cyan fringe along the figure's edge that reads as misregistration - and at seed 5150 the skin carries a genuine tonal flesh screen whose dots darken and crowd into the shading. That is a large improvement on the control. But the Ben-Day screen as the COLOUR MECHANISM does not arrive reliably: at 1.2 the coat carries a proper tonal screen at seed 5150 and almost none at 314159, and at 1.5 the dots become uniform polka dots printed on the garment at every seed tested - the same noun-as-object failure as the control, moved off the frame and onto the coat. Four seeds, six strengths. Left weak deliberately: reach for this for the INK, not for the print. ROUTING BLOCKER: engine=anime on this card, LoRA is qwen-based. studio/_tools/lora_rescue.py; studio/samples/lora_rescue/.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject. studio/_tools/style_examples.py
